title: ChirpNeighbors — San Diego-first regional asset pack
status: Research-backed prioritization proposal; not user approval of each species or a claim of sightings at the user home.
scope: San Diego coastal-slope urban/suburban and habitat-edge yards first; county mountain/desert and coastal wetlands are separate expansions. No exact home coordinates used.

contexts.description: Marine-influenced coastal urban/suburban yard: smaller planted canopy, walls, patios, native border and nonnative ornamentals. Marine low-cloud variant; do not convert to a rainforest.
Warmer inland valley suburb: irrigated garden islands, dry open ground, hotter afternoon state; water availability drives greenness separately from calendar.
Canyon/foothill edge: connected coastal sage scrub or chaparral; ground birds require cover and unpaved substrate. Not every urban lot is this habitat.
Optional mature-tree/woodland or stream-influenced yard: shade, oak litter, moist pocket. Do not fill dry slopes with riparian plants.
Managed containers and indoor plants: lighting, shelter and irrigation govern state; no automatic rain, wind, leaf fall or visiting wild birds indoors.

weather_and_plant_states.render: soft cool light and reduced contrast; inland clear alternative; overcast does not mean rain.
dry grass/seedheads, thinner drought-deciduous foliage, tan soil and persistent evergreen shrubs; plant-specific exceptions such as fuchsia flowers.
retained greens/flowers according to species; do not brown every asset merely because it is July.

weather_and_plant_states.applies: Actual inland heat or offshore dry-wind event

toyon fruit and buckwheat rust heads where appropriate; no universal orange canopy. Deciduous ornamental color is asset specific.
disabled for ordinary coastal/inland San Diego lowland yard default.
